title: Backout (modded-nanogpt port): ln_f and the head read the final residual stream minus a learned scalar (init 0.5) times the stream after block 4 of 6, on the 191-claude incumbent (9,557,761 params, +1)
description: Idea ID: P09-family (a learned scalar gate on a residual path; no backlog entry names this mechanism), under program.md's focus 1 as a port of modded-nanogpt's Backout, which the table has not tried: the state handed to ln_f/head (and to the pretraining-only MTP module) becomes x_6 - lambda * x_4, where x_4 is the residual stream after the fourth of the six Peri-LN blocks (2/3 depth as in the speedrun, whose current train_gpt.py initialises the coefficient at -0.5) and lambda is one learned scalar initialised at 0.5, trained by AdamW with the other auxiliary parameters and kept in the handed-off model for RL. Blocks 1-4 can then write features that later attention needs (statement parsing, bracket and line bookkeeping, citation keys) without the readout having to read around them, which should give the last two blocks' rule-application writes a larger share of what the head sees and make the readout less sensitive to the longer contexts of the 7+ line proofs that expert iteration has to extend to. The only open registration, 195-claude (lean-x0-skip), adds input-embedding skips before every block; this touches only the readout input and does not duplicate it.
hypothesis: Under Peri-LN each of the 12 branch writes enters the residual stream at unit scale times a learned gain, so by the last block about two thirds of the stream was written by blocks 1-4, whose job includes building context features for later attention (what each statement token is, which bracket span it sits in, which line defined a name). ln_f normalises the whole sum and the 107-way head must find the next-token evidence inside it. Backout gives the readout a one-parameter way to cancel the mid-depth state: at lambda = 0.5 the head sees 0.5 * (embedding + writes of blocks 1-4) + writes of blocks 5-6, so late writes weigh twice as much relative to early ones, and gradient descent can move lambda either way (lambda = 0 is exactly the incumbent's function). In modded-nanogpt this was a small gain at equal loss. For this metric the bet is about what the readout depends on when expert iteration moves to longer proofs: context-building features shift with proof length (more lines, more names, longer distances), the rule-application features written late should shift less, so a readout leaning on the late writes should degrade less at 7+ lines and need less re-fitting by the RL fine-tune. Reasons it may do nothing: lambda is one scalar, while ln_f's gain/bias and the head already re-weight directions; Peri-LN's learned output gains can already scale each block's write; and the other speedrun skip-path ports, 114 (U-net skips) and 121 (value embeddings), were both within noise. Per seed the initialisation and data order equal 191's (the new parameter is built from a constant and consumes no random numbers), so paired seed differences isolate the change up to GPU nondeterminism and wall-clock step counts. Decision rule fixed now: this adds code (one parameter, 12 insertions), so no simplicity tolerance applies: keep only if the 3-seed mean is strictly above 191's 683.67, otherwise discard. If another agent keeps a file first, record.py's rule applies.
expected_delta: -20 to +25 vs 191's 683.7 (central +2); keep needs a 3-seed mean > 683.67. Pretraining 5,100-5,500 steps in 300 s per seed (central 5,300; per-step cost unchanged: bench 20.2 steps/s from 45 to 60 s vs 191's bench ~20.8; 191: 5,362/5,298/5,220), ~4.7 epochs; final val loss 0.078-0.095, last train loss 0.035-0.065; learned lambda at handoff (stats.backout, also in every curve point) between 0.15 and 0.9 on every seed; held-out greedy after pretraining 0.955-0.98 (191: 0.9705/0.972/0.9585); round-1 RL targets solved 200-800 (191: 682/454/225, a noisy start that 190/191 showed is recoverable); round-4 RL-solved 1,130-1,200 (191: 1,189/1,160/1,142); handoff n_params 9,557,761 exactly; RL sampling 150-300 samples/s on a healthy pod (the handoff forward adds one subtraction per decoded token), totals 1,700-2,100 s of 2,400. Falsifiers: lambda within 0.05 of 0 at handoff on 2+ seeds says the model rejects the backout (any score difference is then noise); lambda outside [0, 1] or a final val loss above 0.10 on any seed says it destabilises the readout; a 3-seed mean below 660 says it hurts expert iteration; RL round-1 sampling below ~100 samples/s on all three seeds says the slow sampling seen in the bench comes from this file, not the pod.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, the 191-claude model plus Backout: one learned scalar subtracts a fraction of the residual stream after block 4 from the final stream before ln_f/head
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 191-claude: ALiBiGPT gains one scalar parameter `backout` (init BACKOUT_INIT = 0.5); features() keeps the residual stream after block index BACKOUT_BLOCK = 3 (the fourth block) and returns x_final - backout * x_mid, which forward() passes to ln_f and head and mtp_loss passes to the MTP module (it reads the same state as the readout, as before). stats and every curve point record the current value as `backout`. Blocks, widths, heads, ALiBi slopes, MTP module and weight, Muon/AdamW, no-warmup wall-clock cosine, init rule, token batches (TOK_BUDGET 18,432), per-block compile, CUDA-graphed Muon step and handoff unchanged. 12 insertions, 3 deletions.
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,761 = 191's 9,557,760 + 1 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107, and bench_pretrain on an A40 both reported 9,557,761; per Peri-LN block 1,579,136 = qkv 443,520 + proj 147,840 + fc1 492,800 + fc2 491,904 + 4 LayerNorms 3,072; emb + head 82,176; ln_f 768; backout 1). MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff as since 136-fable): 1,875,584, unchanged; pretraining trains 11,433,345 in total; the harness caps the handed-off model's parameters (9.56M), which is what RL and eval use
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; the state_dict has one new 0-d key `backout`; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged cache code (caches[0] holds key positions); backout is per token inside one forward call (x_mid and x_final belong to the same new tokens), so it needs no cache state. CPU check on this file (random init, B=3, T=40, a 17-token prefix then one token at a time through the fork's cache path with pos/mask/caches): cached vs full max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 (191: 1.4e-6); setting lambda to 0 changes logits by up to 0.48, i.e. the term is live and lambda = 0 is the incumbent forward; dL/dlambda is nonzero

backout.formula: h = x_after_block_6 - lambda * x_after_block_4; logits = head(ln_f(h))
backout.optimizer: pretraining AdamW auxiliary group (lr 1e-3 on the shared cosine, wd 0.1, like the LayerNorm gains)
backout.applies_to: the input of ln_f/head and of the pretraining-only MTP module (one code path, features())
backout.in_rl: kept in the handed-off model; the harness's AdamW trains it with the rest of model.parameters()
backout.source: KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt speedrun (Backout); train_gpt.py on master, fetched 2026-09-28, folds it into its post-loop residual mix with initial coefficient -0.5 on a cached mid-depth stream of an 11-layer model. Block choice here (4 of 6 = 2/3 depth) and the separate scalar are my port, not a copy of their code

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock from step 1, no warmup: lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget (setup and per-block compile included, so the first step runs at ~0.99 x peak after ~30-35 s), ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor. Removed: 186's 200-step linear warmup (lr = 1e-3 * step / 200 for step < 200)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same cosine fraction as AdamW from step 1, no warmup (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm; the new backout scalar joins this AdamW group (lr 1e-3, wd 0.1)
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760; plus the backout scalar under AdamW (handed-off total 9,557,761)

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged (the 200-step warmup those runs had is removed in 191, see optimizer.schedule). The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.compile: per-block torch.compile(dynamic=True), coalesce_tiling_analysis off, undone at handoff; Muon step as one CUDA graph; fused AdamW; batch max length from host
config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0; backout scalar 0.5 (a constant, consumes no random numbers)

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence), 2026-09-28 13:27-13:40 BST (432 s of that waiting for A40 capacity and boot), on this pretrain.py before its two stats lines (`backout` in stats and in curve points) were added, so the training and sampling computation is the registered one: 420 steps in 60.3 s, first step at 36 s (191's bench: 30 s; slower setup on this pod), step 2 at 39 s, 117 at 45 s, 420 at 60 s, i.e. 20.2 steps/s from 45 to 60 s (191's bench ~20.8), peak 7.61 GB (191: 7.43), n_params 9,557,761, val loss 0.0831 at 60 s (195-claude's probe 0.082, 193's 0.0846), sample_acc 0.0176 on 4,096 samples, dynamo 3 unique graphs, torch 2.9.1+cu129. Anomaly: sampling ran at 41 samples/s, against 114-266 in every earlier probe (191: 194). The handoff forward adds one subtraction per decoded token and pretraining on the same pod ran at the normal rate, so I attribute this to the pod's CPU / Lean gate (the slow-gate pod pathology of 187/189/192, where sampling fell to 90-142 samples/s with normal pretraining speed), but I did NOT confirm it with a second probe: A40 capacity was scarce (six capacity retries) and the launch window is fixed. If it is the file, all three seeds will sample slowly in RL round 1 and the run will time out; that is registered as a falsifier. CPU smoke of pretrain() on the final file (1,500 records, 20 s budget, fork 51604b3) ran end to end with `backout` in stats and in every curve point (0.4990 after 3 steps); make -C code check clean
config.init_rng: identical to 191's per seed: torch.nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.5)) draws nothing, and model, MTP module and orthogonal-init loop are constructed in the same order, so embeddings, readout, hidden matrices and both data-order generators match 191 seed for seed
